decisions.reason: Product A is close to the firm's established decorative fabrics, so existing knowledge supports recognizing and applying market feedback, making a drop unlikely.
Product B builds on the firm's existing transparent fabric capabilities, allowing effective learning from early results and refinement.
Product C is close to the established burnout fabric range, giving the firm high absorptive capacity to interpret feedback and improve it.
Product D builds on the firm's upholstery fabric knowledge, enabling assimilation of customer feedback and continued improvement.
Product E extends the firm's fabric know-how into flame-retardant variants, and the firm can leverage its related expertise to interpret results and refine the product.
Product F builds on established lining fabric capabilities, so the firm can learn from early market response and apply its existing knowledge to keep it competitive.
